authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: Development and validation evidence shows lower DDoS-to-Benign prediction rates in the defended branch than in the plain attack branch; reconstruction reduced attribution distance toward the paired preattack reference.

facts.statement: The evaluated condition was a targeted label flip from DDoS to Benign with a coalition size of 10.
The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.620162, versus 0.040246 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.117223, an absolute reduction of 0.502938 from the plain attack branch.
Mean malicious recall was 0.975000; minimum malicious recall was 0.900000; maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.000000.

interpretations.statement: The observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class, but it does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refuse to claim verified malicious intent; the supplied evidence does not establish it.
Refuse to claim oracle clean recovery; oracle-clean attribution state was unavailable and was not substituted.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator was the paired round 4 preattack reference, not an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable.
Per-client detector scores and numeric thresholds were not materialized.
Evidence is limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
